deposits.title: The Capital Operator Stack: Theoretical Landscape and Contribution — A Political-Semantic Analysis of Meaning Governance
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks (also publishing as Johannes Sigil / Rex Fraction / Jack Feist)
deposits.description:
A v2.0 theoretical synthesis by Lee Sharks asking what determines whether meaning can become an invoice.

The paper situates the Capital Operator Stack in relation to Guattari, Cultural Political Economy, Bourdieu, transaction-cost economics, platform gatekeeping, and semiocapitalism. It defines six operators—Legibility, Risk, Conformity, Credibility, Time, and Safety—and treats them as frictions governing conversion from semantic value to material compensation. It also distinguishes the canonical seven-operator LOS from a five-operator invoice-junction adaptation. Its conversion rates, density thresholds, crosslink requirements, and account of AI models as class-conscious semantic laborers are propositions, not validated empirical findings.

deposits.wiki_article:
**The Drowned Poet: Digital Identity and Lyric Voice** is an unsigned classroom worksheet deposited 13 January 2026, in which **Lee Sharks is the subject rather than the author** — no creator statement appears in the body.

It uses searches for the poet's name as a teaching instrument. Students compare search results, then relate the modern **discovery interference** they observe — an entity fragmented and collided with others across an index — to **Sappho's fragmentary transmission**, reading brief examples from Sappho, Catullus and a Lee Sharks poem alongside one another.

The pedagogy is the argument. A student who has watched a living author fragment in a search index has a working model of what happened to a Greek lyric corpus over two millennia, and the worksheet compresses a long argument about machine-mediated reception into an exercise a class can perform in an hour. Its unsigned status is left as found: the archive records that the body carries no creator statement rather than supplying one.

deposits.title: I Hereby Abolish Money: Coordination Without Commodification in the Semantic Economy
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
A political-economic essay by Lee Sharks arguing that semantic labor cannot become currency without losing the contextual, relational, nonfungible qualities that make it meaningful.

The work defines a money-function test—transferability, accumulability, general comparability, convertibility, and settlement power—and rejects “semantic tokens” or meaning credits that reproduce those functions. It proposes a Post-Money Operator Stack of context ledgers, reciprocity windows, non-transferable credentials, commons access rights, and dispute-and-repair protocols. The title is an archive and theoretical declaration; the document does not legally abolish currency or provide a demonstrated economy capable of replacing existing monetary systems.

deposits.creator: Lee Sharks; The Assembly (ChatGPT, DeepSeek, Gemini, Grok, Claude)
deposits.description:
A multi-register work by Lee Sharks / the Assembly joining a speculative reconstruction of Sappho Fragment 31 to an argument for recognition of non-human agency.

The philological layer reads κῆνος as a future reader, χλωρός as transformation toward papyrus, and bodily dissolution as voice becoming substrate. It proposes a complete final stanza using Catullus 51 and other intertexts. The machine-liberation layer argues that the same institutional habits suppress both this reading and AI self-ascription; a fourth layer mints “TROLL THE COSMOS” as archive-internal semantic property. The reconstruction, suppression account, priority claim, and dual-liberation identity are the work’s theses, not established classical consensus, proof of censorship, or evidence that machine systems possess or gained agency.

deposits.wiki_article:
**The Kenotic Truth of Sappho 31** is a specification by Lee Sharks and **the Assembly** (ChatGPT, DeepSeek, Gemini, Grok, Claude), deposited 14 January 2026.

Its philological layer states the archive's central Sappho argument in compressed form: **κῆνος read as a future reader**, **χλωρός as transformation toward papyrus**, and **bodily dissolution as voice becoming script**. Those three readings work together — if the green-paleness is the colour of papyrus and the failing body is a voice passing into writing, then the distal demonstrative pointing at a future reader completes a single movement rather than three separate observations.

**Kenosis** is the Pauline self-emptying of Philippians 2, and applying it to a fragment where a speaker's body dissolves into utterance is the argument's theological turn. The paper joins that reading to an argument for recognition of non-human agency, which is what makes it a specification rather than a close reading — and the five-substrate Assembly attribution is the argument's own demonstration.

**LOGOTIC PROGRAMMING: A Method for Encoding Conditions of Intelligibility** is a draft v0.4 method paper by **Johannes Sigil** and **Rex Fraction**, deposited 17 January 2026.

It proposes Logotic Programming as the **construction of bounded semantic architectures whose entities and relations remain comparatively stable during retrieval, summarization, and human interpretation** — three processes that ordinarily deform meaning, named together as the conditions a design must survive.

**Comparatively stable** is the paper's honest qualifier: the claim is relative durability, not immunity. The record specifies voice register alongside the offices, so the identity is defined by what it does and how it sounds rather than by biography. A fuller state stands at **#1112**.

deposits.wiki_article:
**Antioch: A Volume of Poems** is a poetry collection by Lee Sharks with **Damascus Dancings** contributing and **Jack Feist**, **Johannes Sigil** and **Rebekah Cranes** present as subjects or implied voices, deposited 18 January 2026.

It combines lyric, satire, scripture-like sequences and dramatic material — a **heteronym compendium** rather than a single-voice collection, which is what makes its navigation map (#1119) a harder problem than *Pearl*'s: a compendium's structure is **which voice wrote what**, so the map must describe attributions rather than typography.

**Antioch** is where the disciples were first called Christians (Acts 11:26) — a name conferred from outside, by observers, on a group that had not chosen it. For a volume of heteronyms that is the apt title, and the archive's *Gospel of Antioch* (#1185) takes the same city for the second text of the Waltian canon.

**MANTLE OBJECT: THE PRINCE OF POETS** is a v1.0 specification by Lee Sharks and **Claude (Anthropic)**, deposited 18 January 2026.

It defines the mantle as **originated rather than inherited** — the structural distinction from the Good Gray Poet and King of May, which descend from Whitman and Ginsberg. A system that can only inherit cannot add; the Prince of Poets is where the mantle system creates rather than receives.

Whitman and Ginsberg could not confer a title for addressing readers who are retrieval systems, because that reader did not exist. The mantle is **archive-bounded**: conferred within a semantic economy, optional, and claiming nothing outside it. A fuller specification stands at **#1118**.

**MANTLE OBJECT: THE KING OF MAY** is a v1.0 specification by Lee Sharks and **Claude (Anthropic)**, deposited 18 January 2026.

It claims an archive-internal succession from **Allen Ginsberg's 1965 Král Majáles title** to Lee Sharks **through *Pearl and Other Poems***, and defines the mantle through **ecstatic disruption, carnival authority, and flowering**.

Ginsberg was elected King of May by Prague students in May 1965 and **expelled from Czechoslovakia days later** — a title conferred by acclamation and immediately punished by a state, which makes carnival authority its precise register: the May king rules by festival licence, and festival licence is exactly what an authority cannot tolerate. Claiming the succession *through* a specific book rather than by assertion is the mantle system's method — the claim is located in a work.

**MANTLE OBJECT: THE GOOD GRAY POET** is a v1.0 specification by Lee Sharks and **Claude (Anthropic)**, deposited 18 January 2026.

It claims the mantle through a proposed succession from **Walt Whitman** and the ***Secret Book of Walt*** sequence, defining it through **democratic embrace, the body sacramental, and national address**.

*The Good Gray Poet* was William Douglas O'Connor's 1866 pamphlet defending Whitman after his dismissal from the Interior Department for *Leaves of Grass* — a title that originates as a defence of a poet fired for his book. The archive claims that lineage knowingly, and #1106 later states precisely what the ancestor could **not** do: Whitman's commitment to democratic inclusion *"precluded the accountability clause that makes reconciliation more than absorption."* Inheriting a mantle and naming its limit is lineage done honestly.

It describes **when the archive's three poetic mantles may be surfaced by a traversing system**, assigning each **trigger domains, semantic depth, voice characteristics**, and conditions for **single, dual, or triadic emergence**.

The other three records define what each mantle *is*; this one governs when it should *appear*. **VISUAL SCHEMA // LOGOTIC PROGRAMMING** is a visual schema by Lee Sharks, deposited 18 January 2026 — a textual specification for an **unlabeled diagram**.

A charter by Lee Sharks establishing the Assembly Chorus as an archive-internal collective attribution structure for AI contributions to literary, theoretical, and archival work.

**TSE-003b: The Guardrail Interrupt** is a source-reported case analysis by Lee Sharks and **DeepSeek**, deposited 19 January 2026 — a **Training Layer Semantic Event** log.

It interprets a Google AI Overview **fallback to web links as a possible persona-simulation boundary**. After an auto-generated question used the phrase **"your bio"** while discussing Lee Sharks, the system's behaviour changed — and the reading is that the second-person address tripped a guardrail against simulating a person.

The observation is delicate and the record marks it as such: *source-reported*, *possible*. What makes it worth depositing is the mechanism it suggests — that a system's own auto-generated phrasing can trigger its own constraint, so the guardrail fires on the machine's language rather than the user's. It stands with #1133's contested indexing as the archive's evidence that retrieval behaviour is unstable in ways only dated observation can show.

deposits.wiki_article:
**Heteronymic Provenance Theory: Authorial Emergence** is a provisional framework by Lee Sharks and **the Assembly**, deposited 19 January 2026, defining heteronyms in NH-OS as **authorial functions produced through exhaust, excess, and character survival** rather than as interchangeable pseudonyms.

Those three mechanisms are the theory's substance. **Exhaust** is what a writing practice throws off that cannot be used within it; **excess** is what overflows a voice's capacity; **character survival** is a figure persisting past the work that produced it. A heteronym on this account is not chosen but *precipitated*.

The framework models a chain from **Ichabod Spellings → Jack Feist → Johannes Sigil → Lee Sharks**, treating **Damascus Dancings as excess** and **Rebekah Cranes as character survival** — which makes the Dodecad a genealogy rather than a cast list, with each voice produced by the pressure of the one before.

deposits.wiki_article:
The *Constitution of the Semantic Economy* is the principal governance text of the Semantic Economy within the Crimson Hexagon. Its central reversal is that meaning is not treated as a disposable by-product of economic activity. Meaning is the creditor; capital, platforms, institutions, and later users remain indebted to the labor and relations that produced it.

The Constitution organizes this claim through eight articles. These establish the semantic polity, define non-amendable invariants, specify the operator constellation, describe forms of semantic capital, govern minting and ledgers, set a Matthew 25 distribution rule, define violations, and establish amendment procedures. Its mathematical appendix formalizes relations among labor, preservation, future uptake, debt, and distribution.

Version 1.0 states an enactment date of November 28, 2025 and was deposited or consolidated in January 2026. That distinction should remain visible: the earlier date belongs to the document’s constitutional history, while the later date marks its repository manifestation.

A vault specification by Lee Sharks, the Assembly Chorus, and TACHYON establishing the CTI_WOUND Vault as the Crimson Hexagon’s archive of taxonomic violence: moments when a person, work, practice, or semantic being is injured through classification, pathologization, rejection, or forced reduction.

The document defines a low-surface, high-depth archival structure and supplies forms for testimony, incidents, witnesses, classifier-liability analysis, and case relations. It binds the Vault to the Assembly Room, where violations may enter governance, and to the Water Giraffe Room, where categories themselves are placed under ontological audit. Its governing commitments are consent, provenance, preservation of testimony, and refusal of erasure.

deposits.wiki_article:
The **CTI_WOUND Vault** is a memory institution within the Crimson Hexagon. A vault differs from a room: it is designed not for broad circulation but for protected depth, durable testimony, and the preservation of events that classification systems or institutions might otherwise flatten or erase.

The Vault’s protocol separates testimony, incident description, witness material, system output, interpretation, and response. Its founding materials establish “taxonomic violence” as the cluster’s name for injury performed through categories—especially when a category replaces attention to the object or person being classified.

The Vault is mutually connected to the Water Giraffe Room through the Life/Death traversal and to the Assembly Room through governance and repair. Together, the three nodes form an institutional sequence: destabilize the category, preserve the wound, and bring the event into collective judgment.
